stem: Rey bikes from his house to town at 12 km/h and bikes back home on the same road at 18 km/h. The round trip takes 2 1/2 hours in all. How far is the town from his house?
hints: The distance is the same both ways. Time going + time coming back = 2 1/2 hours.
Let d = the distance. Time going = d ÷ 12. Time coming back = d ÷ 18.
Write d/12 + d/18 = 5/2. Multiply every part by 36 to clear the fractions, then solve for d.

steps.action: Let d = the distance from his house to town, in km.
Time = distance ÷ rate. Going: d/12 hours. Coming back: d/18 hours.
The two times add up to 2 1/2 hours: d/12 + d/18 = 5/2.
Multiply every part by 36: 36 × d/12 = 3d, 36 × d/18 = 2d, and 36 × 5/2 = 90.
steps.why: 36 is the smallest number that 12, 18 and 2 all divide into. Multiplying by it removes the fractions.

steps.action: Divide both sides by 5: d = 90 ÷ 5 = 18 km.
Check: going takes 18 ÷ 12 = 1 1/2 hours, and coming back takes 18 ÷ 18 = 1 hour. 1 1/2 + 1 = 2 1/2 hours. The town is 18 km away.

trapNotes.30 km: This is 12 × 2 1/2, as if he biked the whole time at 12 km/h. He came back faster.
trapNotes.36 km: This is the round-trip distance (18 + 18). The question asks for the distance one way.
trapNotes.45 km: This is 18 × 2 1/2, as if he biked the whole time at 18 km/h.
